comments: 2026-02-10 - Initial ticket created. Background: Multiple enterprise customers asked for predictable private deployment upgrade windows and a clearer SLA handoff when moving from hosted to private. Objective is to produce a quarterly slice map that sequences feature rollouts and upgrades across Private/VPC/On-prem customers while minimizing blast radius.

2026-02-14 - Alignment meeting with Engineering, SRE, and Security. Agreed to slice by: SLA tier (Gold/Silver/Bronze), deployment topology (VPC-managed vs on-prem self-hosted), and customer size (<=2 nodes, 3-16 nodes, >16 nodes). Action: Eng to provide perf/upgrade estimate for each slice.

2026-02-18 - Product decision: prioritize customers on Gold SLA with VPC-managed topology for Q2 pilot to validate rollback and monitoring. Rationale: highest revenue and easiest network path for remote runbooks. Noted trade-off: slower time-to-wide-release for on-prem customers.

2026-02-20 - Engineering update (ENG-4391): Parallel upgrade path requires extra work on KV cache migration logic and may increase short-term risk of token misalignment. Staged rollout reduces risk but increases lift. Estimate: parallel + canary automation = 8 dev+qa sprints; staged = 5 sprints but manual oversight required. Asking product to choose risk vs time trade-off.

2026-02-24 - Security note: KMS key rotation testing must be included in canary flow. HSM customers require extra validation windows; propose scheduling on separate slice to avoid blocking VPC rollouts.

2026-02-27 - PM decision: Run a hybrid approach for Q2 pilot — parallel upgrades for Gold/VPC customers with automated canaries + immediate rollback hooks; staged manual rollouts for on-prem/HSM customers in Q3. Updated timeline and comms plan to reflect hybrid approach.

2026-02-27 - Next steps documented: finalize canary metrics (error rate, head latency P95, failed token reconciliation), capture runbook template, and coordinate customer communications for pilot opt-in. Owner assignments added to action items.
description:
Background:
Many enterprise customers have asked for more predictable Private/VPC/on-prem upgrade sequencing and clear SLAs when moving off hosted. This ticket creates a quarterly 'slice map' — a prioritized schedule and rollout plan for Private features, upgrade windows, and compliance-sensitive validations so customers can plan migrations and internal approvals.

Goal:
- Deliver a validated Q2 pilot rollouts plan that reduces customer upgrade uncertainty and supports Gold-tier customers with clear SLA commitments.
- Produce a repeatable slice map artifact that the PM/Eng/SRE teams can reuse for subsequent quarters.

Success metrics:
- Pilot customers (>=5 Gold/VPC accounts) complete an upgrade with zero data loss and <=1% increase in 95th percentile latency during canaries.
- Time-to-resolution for rollback events <= 30 minutes for canary slices.
- Published customer timeline and acceptance form with at least 3 enterprise sign-ups for Q2 pilot.

Scope (in):
- Sequence and schedule for Q2 pilot (Gold/VPC), including canary metric set and rollback playbook.
- Engineering acceptance criteria and test matrix for KV cache/quantization compatibility during upgrades.
- Communications package for customers and account teams.

Out of scope (for Q2 pilot):
- Full on-prem automated upgrade automation (deferred to Q3).
- New billing model changes.

Key milestones and dates:
- 2026-02-18: Slice criteria finalized (done)
- 2026-02-22: Engineering estimates reviewed (in-progress)
- 2026-03-05: Canary plan and SRE runbook draft
- 2026-03-20: Tech validation with internal staging clusters
- 2026-04-01: Customer opt-in portal live and comms distributed
- 2026-05-15: Pilot upgrades completed and postmortem published

Decisions & trade-offs:
- Hybrid rollout approach selected: parallel automated canaries for Gold/VPC customers; staged manual rollouts for on-prem/HSM customers. Trade-off favors faster validation with highest-value customers while deferring higher-risk topologies to a later quarter.
- To minimize regression risk during parallel upgrades we will require a short-lived compatibility layer for older runtime kernels; this increases short-term engineering effort but reduces customer-facing risk.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: KV cache incompatibility leads to token misordering in long-running chat sessions. Mitigation: enforce prefix validation gates and roll forward only after KV checksum pass in canary windows.
- Risk: HSM customers impose maintenance windows that don't align with Q2 cadence. Mitigation: schedule HSM rollouts in Q3 slice and publish SLA exceptions.
- Risk: Customer confusion about opt-in vs automatic upgrades. Mitigation: explicit opt-in portal and targeted AE communication; trial customers on pilot list will be contacted by Solutions Eng.

Stakeholders and approvals needed:
- Eng (Serving Runtime): signoff on KV migration approach (ENG-4391).
- SRE: runbook and SLO adjustments.
- Security: KMS/HSM validation checklist and approval.
- Sales & Customer Success: customer comms + opt-in coordination.

Artifacts & links:
- Slice map draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/Private-Q2-Slice-Map
- PRD: https://drive.redwood.ai/rdw-private-prd-v2.pdf
- Engineering RFCs and PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deployments/pulls/1284
- Pilot opt-in form mock: https://drive.redwood.ai/private-pilot-optin-mock.png

Communication plan:
- 2-week cadence updates to AEs and pilot customers.
- Public-facing timeline page when opt-in portal is live.
- Post-pilot postmortem and KB entry for runbook.

Notes for the next iteration (Q3):
- Automate on-prem upgrade path and HSM validations.
- Add cost-estimate tooling to the Console to show expected burst capacity costs for dedicated pools during upgrades.

If you are an owner on any action item above, please add a comment with ETA and any blockers.
